why: In figures 1 and 5 the grey panel is on the right, the arrow is on the left, and a small black circle sits next to a white circle. Figures 3 and 4 are the mirror image of these: grey panel on the left, arrow on the right, with a white circle and a small black circle side by side. So every figure has two separate circles, one white and one black. Figure 2 has the arrow and panel in the right places, but it shows only one big black circle and no white circle. That is why figure 2 is the odd one out.
trick: Count the small parts in every figure first (circles, arrows, panels). The figure with a missing or merged part is usually the odd one.
note: Figure 2 may be a black circle covering the white one; gradients in the original were drawn as flat grey/black. Mirror-image reading makes 1,3,4,5 consistent.
